## Inputs and record reconciliation

Original CSV exports and supplied Excel workbooks are preserved in `Data/APEX/`.
The Figure 1B chunk below automatically refreshes `Data/APEX/derived/` when
source files change (using `scripts/import_apex_records.py`). Identical copies are collapsed; conflicting readings are
reported separately and never averaged. The original notebook is retained at
`Data/APEX/ACE21_Sensor_data_legacy.Rmd` for provenance.

## Approved logger-removal exclusions

The investigator identified May 1–15, 2017 measurements for tanks 1–4 as invalid
because the loggers were removed. Six isolated measurements on April 17–19 were
also identified as logger-removal/cleaning interruptions. Exact tank/time pairs
are listed in the plotting script. Source measurements are never overwritten.
Excluded rows are exported to audit tables under `Data/APEX/derived/`.

## Official Figure 1B: treatment means and SE

The display runs March 20–May 17, using the first/last dated PAM sampling files.
The x-axis shows elapsed days, with March 20 as day 0; dates remain in the saved data.
Means and SE are calculated across available tanks at each timestamp. There is
no averaging across time or interpolation. SE is not displayed for n < 2.

```{r figure-1b-temperature, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.5}
source("scripts/plot_apex_temperature.R")
```

This prints the plot and saves PDF, PNG, and editable RDS versions in `Figures/`.
The compact vector panel is exported to `Figures/assets/Fig1/Fig1B_temperature.pdf`.
The map and trait table do not belong in this temperature-data notebook.
Run **`ACE21_Figure1.Rmd`** to assemble A, B, and C and save `Figures/Fig1.pdf`
and `Figures/Fig1.png`. Its assembly chunk imports this exported vector panel;
it does not recalculate or duplicate temperature methods.

For a command-line build of the whole figure, run `scripts/build_figure1.py`
with Python containing openpyxl, reportlab, and pypdf. The figure also requires
Rscript and Poppler (pdftoppm). `FIGURE1_PYTHON` can select the Python executable
when running from R.
